records.finalText: I got a lot out of that book I read.
records.rationale: Got a lot out of a book is a natural benefit idiom and the relative clause identifies a completed reading experience.

records.originalText: Having read the book, I could answer all the questions.
records.finalText: Having read the book, I could answer all the questions.
records.rationale: The completed reading participle correctly shares its subject with the main question-answering clause.

records.originalText: I remember reading the book.
records.finalText: I remember reading the book.
records.rationale: Remember reading correctly uses a gerund to refer to a memory of a completed activity.

records.originalText: When you're done with the book, put it back where you found it.
records.finalText: When you're done with the book, put it back where you found it.
records.rationale: Done with the book and put it back form a natural conditional instruction with an explicit object and location condition.

records.originalText: No one can read the book without crying.
records.finalText: No one can read the book without crying.
records.rationale: The assertion that nobody can read the book without crying is an unqualified universal emotional-response claim.

records.originalText: Bring the book to me, not to Tom.
records.finalText: Bring the book to me, not to Tom.
records.rationale: The book request identifies the object and contrasts two explicit recipients naturally.

records.originalText: He sent me a letter asking if the book had reached me.
records.finalText: He sent me a letter asking if the book had reached me.
records.rationale: The asking-if participle and past-perfect delivery clause form a coherent specific correspondence account.

records.originalText: Are you through with the book?
records.finalText: Are you through with the book?
records.rationale: Through with the book is a natural complete question about finishing an explicitly named reading activity.

records.originalText: That book is familiar to all young children.
records.finalText: That book is familiar to all young children.
records.rationale: All young children is an unbounded population and the supposedly familiar book is not identified.

records.originalText: I found the book so interesting that I kept on reading it until daybreak.
records.finalText: I found the book so interesting that I kept on reading it until daybreak.
records.rationale: So interesting that links a personal book evaluation with continued reading until daybreak naturally.

records.originalText: Sorry, the book is out of stock.
records.finalText: Sorry, the book is out of stock.
records.rationale: Out of stock is a conventional service-availability expression about a specific book.

records.originalText: Orders for the book poured in.
records.finalText: Orders for the book poured in.
records.rationale: Orders poured in is a natural figurative description of a particular book's demand.

records.originalText: There was a flag at the top of the pole.
records.finalText: There was a flag at the top of the pole.
records.rationale: The existential description and at-the-top-of location identify a concrete flag-and-pole scene.

records.originalText: It will take a long time to suppress the revolt.
records.finalText: It will take a long time to suppress the revolt.
records.rationale: Suppress the revolt is a natural complete duration prediction about a specific conflict, without endorsing violence.

records.originalText: The riot was suppressed without difficulty.
records.finalText: The riot was suppressed without difficulty.
records.rationale: The passive suppression account reports a specific past riot outcome without graphic detail or instructions.

records.originalText: The riot was soon put down by the police.
records.finalText: The riot was soon put down by the police.
records.rationale: Repeats 43975's successful riot-suppression event using put down and an explicit police agent.

records.originalText: The little boy is used to talking with grown-ups.
records.finalText: The little boy is used to talking with grown-ups.
records.rationale: Used to talking correctly uses be-used-to plus a gerund for familiarity with speaking to adults.

records.originalText: The law is full of ambiguities.
records.finalText: The law is full of ambiguities.
records.rationale: The law is unidentified, so the claim about ambiguities has no independently assessable legal scope.

records.originalText: The bill passed the Diet.
records.finalText: The bill passed the Diet.
records.rationale: Passed the Diet is a valid specific past legislative-event expression using the Japanese legislature's English name.

records.originalText: Many people are against the bill.
records.finalText: Many people are against the bill.
records.rationale: Against the bill is a natural statement of a contextual group's opposition, without an actual current political assertion.

records.originalText: There is no possibility of the bill being passed.
records.finalText: There is no possibility of the bill being passed.
records.rationale: Possibility of the bill being passed correctly uses a passive gerund to express a speaker's bounded legislative prediction.

records.originalText: The method was crude, but very effective.
records.finalText: The method was crude, but very effective.
records.rationale: Crude but effective is a coherent subjective contrast applied to a specific method.

records.originalText: The method was too expensive to be practical.
records.finalText: The method was too expensive to be practical.
records.rationale: Too expensive to be practical is a natural infinitive-consequence evaluation of a particular method.

records.originalText: The report revealed that many teenagers are alcoholics.
records.finalText: The report revealed that many teenagers are alcoholics.
records.rationale: The unscoped report and unspecified teenage population cannot support an alcoholism prevalence assertion.

records.originalText: The report cannot be true.
records.finalText: The report cannot be true.
records.rationale: Repeats the published rumor-turned-out-false informational-falsity content as an inference about an unidentified report.

records.originalText: The report is utterly false.
records.finalText: The report is utterly false.
records.rationale: Repeats the published informational-falsity proposition with an unidentified report and an intensifier.

records.originalText: The report turned out to be false.
records.finalText: The report turned out to be false.
records.rationale: Pragmatic repeat of the published rumor-turned-out-to-be-false discovery; report replaces the generic information object.

records.originalText: That report was important because it pointed out all the errors the committee had made.
records.finalText: That report was important because it pointed out all the errors the committee had made.
records.rationale: The because and relative clauses clearly explain why a particular committee-error report mattered.

records.originalText: The mother laid her baby on the bed softly.
records.finalText: The mother gently laid her baby on the bed.
records.rationale: Use gently rather than softly with laid a baby for a natural manner collocation without changing the careful placement event.

records.originalText: Because of his great professional skill, the lawyer has a large number of clients.
records.finalText: Because of his great professional skill, the lawyer has a large number of clients.
records.rationale: The stated professional-skill explanation concerns one lawyer's clientele, not a universal business or legal guarantee.

records.originalText: The lawyer has a lot of wealthy clients.
records.finalText: The lawyer has a lot of wealthy clients.
records.rationale: The lawyer's wealthy clients form a specific possession description distinct from the previous causal account.

records.originalText: Don't lean against the wall.
records.finalText: Don't lean against the wall.
records.rationale: Lean against the wall is a natural complete household or public-space prohibition.

records.originalText: The fence will be painted by Tom tomorrow.
records.finalText: The fence will be painted by Tom tomorrow.
records.rationale: The future passive specifies the fence, agent and time in a coherent planned-painting statement.

records.originalText: The soldier refused to fire his rifle at the enemy.
records.finalText: The soldier refused to fire his rifle at the enemy.
records.rationale: Refused to fire correctly takes an infinitive and describes a particular soldier declining a violent action.

records.originalText: The soldiers fought valiantly, but finally they had to give in.
records.finalText: The soldiers fought valiantly, but finally they had to give in.
records.rationale: Fought valiantly and had to give in form a grammatical non-graphic particular battle account.

records.originalText: The document passed into the enemy's hands.
records.finalText: The document passed into the enemy's hands.
records.rationale: Passed into the enemy's hands is a natural idiom for loss of control over a specified document.

records.originalText: The meaning of this sentence is obscure.
records.finalText: The meaning of this sentence is obscure.
records.rationale: Obscure is a natural adjective evaluating the clarity of an explicitly identified sentence's meaning.

records.originalText: It is impossible to resolve the conflict.
records.finalText: It is impossible to resolve the conflict.
records.rationale: Impossible to resolve is a grammatical situated assessment of a particular conflict, without a universal claim.

records.originalText: The surface of the object is fairly rough.
records.finalText: The surface of the object is fairly rough.
records.rationale: Fairly rough naturally describes the degree of a particular object's surface texture.

records.originalText: The scenery is beautiful beyond description.
records.finalText: The scenery is beautiful beyond description.
records.rationale: Beautiful beyond description is a conventional subjective scenery evaluation with a natural degree phrase.

records.originalText: The beauty of the scenery was beyond description.
records.finalText: The beauty of the scenery was beyond description.
records.rationale: Repeats 44175's beautiful-beyond-description scenery assessment, changing only tense and nominalization.

records.originalText: The view is beautiful beyond words.
records.finalText: The view is beautiful beyond words.
records.rationale: Repeats 44175's scenery beauty assessment with view and beyond words as close paraphrases.

records.originalText: There's not enough light in this room for sewing.
records.finalText: There's not enough light in this room for sewing.
records.rationale: Enough light for sewing names the room, resource and activity in a complete practical adequacy statement.

records.originalText: The room is furnished with two beds.
records.finalText: The room is furnished with two beds.
records.rationale: Furnished with two beds is a natural passive-state room description with a concrete quantity.

records.originalText: The room was littered with scraps of paper.
records.finalText: The room was littered with scraps of paper.
records.rationale: Littered with scraps of paper is a natural descriptive collocation about one room's state.

records.originalText: The room is spacious and light.
records.finalText: The room is spacious and light.
records.rationale: Spacious and light are natural complementary room-description adjectives.

records.originalText: The room looks out on the ocean.
records.finalText: The room looks out on the ocean.
records.rationale: Looks out on the ocean is a natural view-related phrasal expression about a specific room.

records.originalText: The room was in perfect order.
records.finalText: The room was in perfect order.
records.rationale: In perfect order is a conventional complete description of a particular room's tidiness.

records.originalText: Nothing in the room matches with anything else.
records.finalText: Nothing in the room matches anything else.
records.rationale: Remove unnecessary with after matches for a more natural direct-object collocation; retain the mismatch among all room furnishings.

records.originalText: The minute I entered the room, they stopped talking.
records.finalText: The minute I entered the room, they stopped talking.
records.rationale: The minute I entered correctly introduces the immediate stopping event with a shared room setting.

records.originalText: The room was bathed in sunshine.
records.finalText: The room was bathed in sunshine.
records.rationale: Bathed in sunshine is a natural figurative room-light description, distinct from room size or furnishings.

records.originalText: The room was empty except for a shabby bed.
records.finalText: The room was empty except for a shabby bed.
records.rationale: Except for a shabby bed gives a concrete exception in a natural room-inventory description.

records.originalText: There was nothing but an old chair in the room.
records.finalText: There was nothing but an old chair in the room.
records.rationale: Nothing but an old chair is a natural restrictive room-inventory description with a distinct furnishing.

records.originalText: The room was devoid of furniture.
records.finalText: The room was devoid of furniture.
records.rationale: Devoid of furniture is a natural formal collocation describing a genuinely unfurnished room.

records.originalText: He made no effort to accept his daughter's boyfriend.
records.finalText: He made no effort to accept his daughter's boyfriend.
records.rationale: Made no effort to accept correctly takes an infinitive and reports a specific family attitude.

records.originalText: The lady wore a necklace of pearls.
records.finalText: The lady wore a necklace of pearls.
records.rationale: A necklace of pearls is a natural material-description phrase in a particular past appearance account.

records.originalText: It was said that that lady was an actress.
records.finalText: It was said that that lady was an actress.
records.rationale: It was said that correctly forms a reporting passive and identifies the reported occupation without endorsing it as fact.

records.originalText: The lady's funeral was held at the local church.
records.finalText: The lady's funeral was held at the local church.
records.rationale: The local-church funeral statement is a specific respectful past event without an unqualified religious claim.

records.originalText: The ladies are looking after the children whose parents are employed in factories during the daytime.
records.finalText: The ladies are looking after the children whose parents are employed in factories during the daytime.
records.rationale: The whose relative clause correctly links children and parents in a coherent factory-work childcare arrangement.

records.originalText: The couple lived a happy life to the end.
records.finalText: The couple lived a happy life to the end.
records.rationale: Lived a happy life to the end is a natural positive particular life-story summary.

records.originalText: The real estate man told lies to the couple.
records.finalText: The real estate agent told lies to the couple.
records.rationale: Use real estate agent for the natural occupational term while retaining the same deception of the couple.

records.originalText: The poor young man finally became a great artist.
records.finalText: The poor young man finally became a great artist.
records.rationale: The past narrative describes a particular disadvantaged young man's later artistic achievement without a universal claim.
